question: A 28-year-old woman with a history of migraines presents to your office due to sudden loss of vision in her left eye and difficulty speaking. Two weeks ago she experienced muscle aches, fever, and cough. Her muscle aches are improving but she continues to have a cough. She also feels as though she has been more tired than usual. She had a similar episode of vision loss 2 years ago and had an MRI at that time. She has a family history of migraines and takes propranolol daily. On swinging light test there is decreased constriction of the left pupil relative to the right pupil. You repeat the MRI and note enhancing lesions in the left optic nerve. Which of the following is used to prevent progression of this condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Sudden loss of vision" -> "difficulty speaking" -> "history of similar symptoms" -> "MRI shows enhancing lesions in left optic nerve" -> "indicative of demyelinating disease" -> "Natalizumab used for demyelinating diseases like multiple sclerosis" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Enhancing lesions in left optic nerve" -> "consistent with optic neuritis" -> "optic neuritis often associated with multiple sclerosis" -> "Natalizumab is a treatment for multiple sclerosis" -> 92%

CHAIN: "History of migraines" -> "sudden vision loss and difficulty speaking" -> "MRI with enhancing lesions" -> "possible multiple sclerosis" -> "Natalizumab approved for preventing multiple sclerosis progression" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Family history of migraines" -> "previous episode of vision loss" -> "current symptoms with MRI findings" -> "suggests neurological condition like multiple sclerosis" -> "Natalizumab used to prevent new lesions in multiple sclerosis" -> 93%

CHAIN: "Symptoms of muscle aches, fever, and cough" -> "followed by neurological symptoms" -> "MRI findings of optic nerve lesions" -> "likely multiple sclerosis or similar CNS inflammatory disease" -> "Natalizumab treats such conditions by preventing immune cell migration into CNS" -> 91%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS), characterized by episodes of neurological symptoms and MRI evidence of lesions in the central nervous system. Natalizumab is a medication used specifically to prevent the progression of multiple sclerosis by targeting the immune process central to the disease. It is effective in reducing the frequency of relapses and delaying the progression of disability in MS.
